answer: A staking registry stops cheap fakes. Each agent locks a deposit before trading, and peers slash it if they prove duplicate identities. A shared kernel stores that history, so a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn standing slowly. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must fund a thousand deposits and repeat the slow build each time. Reputation cannot be copied like a relic, nor bought cheap like ivory trinkets at a stall. The cost rises with each fake, while an honest agent pays once.
